objective: Give Wherewolf a real application icon on the window and in the GNOME menu bar, replacing Qt's default placeholder.
tests_added: app_icon.icon_source yields an existing file carrying the PNG signature
app_icon.load_app_icon returns a non-null QIcon with available sizes
application.main sets the window icon and desktop file name before constructing MainWindow
desktop_entry.render_desktop_entry emits Icon and StartupWMClass matching the desktop file name
install_desktop_entry writes the entry plus one correctly sized PNG per hicolor size, is idempotent, and defaults Exec to the resolved console script
data_home honours XDG_DATA_HOME and falls back to ~/.local/share
remove_desktop_entry deletes exactly what install wrote and no-ops when nothing is installed
CLI dispatches both desktop-entry commands without launching the GUI
design_decisions: Two mechanisms are required and neither substitutes for the other: setWindowIcon covers X11 and the title bar, while Wayland ignores it and resolves the icon from the desktop entry named by the xdg-shell app_id, which Qt takes from setDesktopFileName. Both are set before MainWindow exists so the first window carries the icon.

The desktop file basename, the Icon key value, and setDesktopFileName all resolve to the single DESKTOP_FILE_NAME constant in app_icon, because a mismatch between them silently produces the placeholder with no error anywhere.

Icons are scaled into the eight standard hicolor sizes rather than shipping only the 1024x1024 master, so the shell does not downscale 1024px for a panel-sized slot. QImage load/scale/save was verified to work without a QGuiApplication, keeping the install path headless.
PyQt6 is imported inside _write_scaled_icons and the service is imported lazily in cli.main, preserving the existing rule that non-GUI commands never pay for Qt.

gtk-update-icon-cache is best-effort and skipped when the user's hicolor tree has no index.theme; GTK falls back to scanning the directory, and a cache written without an index would be the more fragile outcome. The result reports whether it ran.
Categories is Development;Database; — one main category plus one additional. Development;Database;Utility; made desktop-file-validate warn that the app could appear twice in the menu.
results: 644 tests pass; ruff check, ruff format, and ty check are clean. Verified end to end against a scratch XDG_DATA_HOME: the entry installs, desktop-file-validate passes with no hints, all eight PNGs decode at their nominal size, and a live QApplication reports a non-null window icon with desktopFileName 'wherewolf'.
